target: fatal accidents involving Boeing commercial jets

evidence.source_title: 2015 Statistical Summary of Commercial Jet Airplane Accidents — Worldwide Operations 1959-2015
evidence.scope: worldwide commercial jet fleet under documented Boeing inclusion/exclusion rules
evidence.observation: The 2015 airplane-accident table contains 28 accidents and identifies three fatal rows through external fatalities: CEIBA 737-800 with seven external fatalities, Air India A319 with one external fatality, and Services Air A310 with eight external fatalities. Boeing defines external fatalities to include fatalities on other aircraft involved. Therefore the only Boeing target member among those three fatal rows is CEIBA.
evidence.use: annual fatal-commercial-jet exhaustion and Boeing membership mapping

evidence.publisher: Bureau d'Enquête et d'Analyse pour la sécurité de l'aviation civile du Sénégal (BEA Sénégal)
evidence.source_title: Rapport final — accident du 05/09/2015 entre B737-800 3C-LLY et HS125-700A 6V-AIM
evidence.scope: event-level authority report; retained public mirror
evidence.observation: The report identifies CEIBA 3C-LLY as Boeing 737-8FB, serial 41157, involved in the mid-air collision with 6V-AIM. Seven occupants of the other aircraft died; the Boeing continued to destination.
evidence.provenance_caveat: The currently retained public copy is a mirror of the Senegal authority final report rather than a canonical live BEA-hosted URL.

evidence.scope: global commercial aviation under IATA methodology
evidence.observation: IATA reports zero fatal jet accidents under its onboard-fatality methodology and explicitly says it does not count fatalities on the ground or on other aircraft not fitting its accident criteria. It separately excludes Germanwings 9525 and Metrojet 9268; both are non-Boeing aircraft and therefore do not alter the BSFM Boeing target-membership result for 2015.
evidence.use: independent scope reconciliation and external-fatality-methodology check

completeness_assessment.reason: Boeing's documented worldwide commercial-jet table exhausts the 2015 fatal rows including external fatalities and maps only CEIBA to Boeing. The Senegal investigation authority confirms the CEIBA collision and aircraft identity. IATA independently explains why onboard-only statistics omit this external-fatality case; the deliberate Germanwings/Metrojet events are non-Boeing and do not create an unresolved Boeing target membership for this year.

gate_effect: 2015 annual G1 cell PASS only; overall G1 remains BLOCKED until every required year passes
